topics.display_title: Congress of Vienna and Concert of Europe

panels.title: Vienna's starting problem
ascii_lines: NAPOLEON DEFEATED -> Europe needs reconstruction
FEAR 1 -> renewed French hegemony
FEAR 2 -> revolutionary and national contagion
VIENNA 1814-15 -> strategic peace plus conservative restoration
MUST REMEMBER: The Congress of Vienna (1814-15) used balance, legitimacy, compensation and
containment after Napoleon; the Concert was a consultation practice among powers rather than
a permanent supranational government.

panels.title: Three settlement principles
ascii_lines: LEGITIMACY -> restore dynasties
BALANCE OF POWER -> contain France with buffers
COMPENSATION -> reward victors with territory
COMMON LIMIT -> populations do not supply consent

panels.title: Northern and central map logic
ascii_lines: NETHERLANDS -> Belgium + Holland buffer France
GERMAN LANDS -> 39-state Confederation under Austria
PRUSSIA -> Rhineland, Westphalia and part of Saxony
SWITZERLAND -> neutrality recognised

panels.title: Italian and Polish deferral
ascii_lines: ITALY -> Austria gets Lombardy and Venetia
PIEDMONT -> strengthened by Genoa
POLAND -> Congress Poland under Russian control
RESULT -> national questions postponed, not resolved
source_references: Italy: Austrian control and Piedmont's strengthening

panels.title: Concert operating mechanism
ascii_lines: GREAT POWERS -> consult rather than fight immediately
CONGRESSES -> periodic management of disputes
STATUS QUO -> territorial and political order defended
LIMIT -> no permanent treaty-state or democratic representation

panels.title: Concert versus Holy Alliance
ascii_lines: CONCERT -> broad practical great-power consultation
HOLY ALLIANCE -> Russia, Austria, Prussia; symbolic conservatism
OVERLAP -> both emerge in 1815 order
RULE -> never use the names as synonyms

panels.title: Reintegration and repression
ascii_lines: AIX 1818 -> France readmitted to consultation
CARLSBAD 1819 -> censorship and university control
EXTERNAL LOGIC -> include a former enemy
INTERNAL LOGIC -> exclude liberal-national dissent

panels.title: Intervention congress sequence
ascii_lines: TROPPAU 1820 -> intervention principle asserted
LAIBACH 1821 -> intervention against revolution applied
VERONA 1822 -> French intervention in Spain approved
AFTER VERONA -> old congress rhythm weakens
source_references: Intervention at Troppau, Laibach and Verona

panels.title: Belgium tests flexibility
ascii_lines: 1815 -> Belgium joined with Holland as buffer
1830 -> Belgian revolt breaks the arrangement
CONCERT -> accepts independence
LESSON -> adaptation can preserve wider equilibrium

panels.title: 1848 pressure and failure
ascii_lines: PRESSURE -> national + liberal + social grievances converge
DIVISION -> liberals, nationalists and workers differ
CONFLICT -> national claims collide in multinational empires
FORCE -> dynastic armies remain loyal and reverse revolutions
CLOSE DISTINCTION: The Vienna settlement's long peace among great powers must be separated
from repression of liberal and national movements and from wars that continued at imperial
or regional margins.
CLOSE DISTINCTION: The Vienna settlement's long peace among great powers must be separated
from repression of liberal and national movements and from wars that continued at imperial
or regional margins.

panels.title: Vienna's unintended gravediggers
ascii_lines: PRUSSIA GAINS RHINELAND -> stronger western base
PIEDMONT GAINS GENOA -> stronger Italian state
VIENNA INTENT -> reinforce conservative balance
LATER RESULT -> strengthened states lead national unification
EVIDENCE LIMIT: Metternich mattered, but British, Russian, Prussian, Austrian, French and
smaller-state interests shaped the settlement; stability was negotiated and adaptive, not
the product of one statesman or a frozen order.

panels.title: Peace-versus-repression spine
ascii_lines: SUCCESS -> no renewed Napoleonic hegemony
METHOD -> balance, reintegration and consultation
COST -> censorship, intervention and denied nationality
VERDICT -> peace among powers, legitimacy deficit among peoples
source_references: Peace, repression and the final verdict
